title: Multi-Floor Smart Parking Lot System
summary: Design an automated multi-floor parking lot with dynamic spot allocation, tiered vehicle types, dynamic fee calculation, and multi-gate entry/exit.
functionalRequirements: The parking lot has multiple floors, each containing different parking spot types: Compact, Regular, Large, and Electric Vehicle (EV).
Supports multiple vehicle types: Motorcycle (Compact), Car (Regular), Truck/Bus (Large), and EV Car (EV spot with charging).
Dynamic Spot Allocation: Supports configurable assignment strategies (e.g., Nearest to Entry, Lowest Floor First).
Entry Gate: Issues an immutable parking ticket recording entry timestamp, allocated spot ID, vehicle number, and gate ID.
Exit Gate: Reads the ticket, calculates the fee based on vehicle type and duration (hourly + peak rate), processes payment, and frees the spot.
Display Board: Each floor displays real-time available spots per spot type.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Thread safety: Multiple entry gates cannot allocate the same parking spot simultaneously.
Extensibility: Adding a new vehicle type (e.g., Heavy Commercial) or new spot strategy must not require rewriting existing parking manager logic (Open-Closed Principle).
High Cohesion: Separation of fee calculation, ticket lifecycle, and physical spot allocation.

criteria.name: Domain Modeling & Entity Decomposition
criteria.description: Decomposes the problem into clean domain entities (Floor, Spot, Vehicle, Ticket, Gate) without leaky abstractions.

criteria.name: Single Responsibility & Cohesion
criteria.description: Classes have focused responsibilities; avoids God classes (e.g., ParkingLot does not calculate fees, print receipts, and manage locks directly).

criteria.name: Coupling & Design Patterns
criteria.description: Effective abstraction using Strategy pattern for Spot Assignment & Pricing, Factory pattern for Spots/Vehicles, and Observer for Display Board.

criteria.name: Extensibility, Concurrency & Trade-offs
criteria.description: Sound reasoning around concurrent spot booking, race conditions, edge cases (lost ticket, full lot), and design trade-offs.

entities.name: ParkingLot
entities.responsibility: Top-level coordinator holding floors and gates

entities.name: ParkingFloor
entities.responsibility: Manages spots of various types on a specific floor

entities.name: ParkingSpot
entities.responsibility: Represents physical slot with status (FREE, OCCUPIED)

entities.name: Vehicle
entities.responsibility: Abstract base vehicle with license plate and vehicle type

entities.name: ParkingTicket
entities.responsibility: Immutable record of vehicle entry, spot, and timestamp

interfaces.name: IDisplayBoardObserver
methods: onSpotStatusChanged(FloorId floor, SpotType type, int availableCount): void

designPatterns.name: Strategy Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Allows swapping spot allocation algorithms (Nearest vs Lowest Floor) without modifying ParkingLot

designPatterns.name: Factory Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Decouples instantiation of various spot types and vehicles

starterTemplate.tradeOffsAndAssumptions: Assuming centralized in-memory lock per floor for spot reservation to prevent double allocation. Tickets are immutable once issued.

title: Multi-Car Elevator Dispatcher System
summary: Design a control system for a high-rise building with multiple elevator cars, handling internal floor selections and external hall calls with optimal dispatching.
functionalRequirements: Building has N floors and M elevator cars.
External Hall Panels: Passengers on any floor can press UP or DOWN call buttons.
Internal Car Panels: Passengers inside a car can select destination floors, trigger door open/close, and press emergency stop.
Elevator Dispatcher: Orchestrates hall calls and assigns the most optimal elevator car based on direction, distance, and current load.
Car States: Cars transition between IDLE, MOVING_UP, MOVING_DOWN, DOOR_OPEN, and MAINTENANCE.
Safety Constraints: Weight sensor prevents moving if overloaded; emergency stop overrides dispatch instructions.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Extensibility: Dispatch algorithm (SCAN/LOOK vs Nearest Car vs Energy-Saving) must be swappable without altering car mechanics.
State Integrity: Elevator cannot transition directly from MOVING_UP to DOOR_OPEN without stopping.
Testability: Elevator movement and dispatch decisions can be simulated deterministically.

criteria.name: State Management & Transitions
criteria.description: Uses State pattern or clear finite state machine to manage elevator car life cycle and safety invariants.

criteria.name: Dispatcher Decoupling & Strategy
criteria.description: Dispatcher strategy is cleanly isolated from physical car hardware interfaces and panel events.

criteria.name: Request & Event Modeling
criteria.description: Distinguishes between internal destination requests and external hall calls with clear prioritization.

criteria.name: Concurrency, Edge Cases & Trade-offs
criteria.description: Addresses starvation of opposing-direction floors, load limits, emergency stops, and thread safety.

entities.name: ElevatorController
entities.responsibility: High-level coordinator of all elevator cars and dispatcher

entities.name: ElevatorCar
entities.responsibility: Represents an individual elevator cabin with state, capacity, and current floor

entities.name: HallButton
entities.responsibility: External floor button to request UP or DOWN ride

entities.name: ElevatorRequest
entities.responsibility: Encapsulates source floor, destination floor, and timestamp

designPatterns.name: State Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Encapsulates behavior for IDLE, MOVING_UP, MOVING_DOWN, and DOOR_OPEN states

designPatterns.name: Strategy Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Permits plugging different scheduling algorithms (LOOK / SCAN / FCFS)

starterTemplate.tradeOffsAndAssumptions: Chose LOOK algorithm over FCFS to minimize wait times and motor wear. Assumes elevator floor arrival triggers an event loop tick.

title: Expense Sharing & Debt Settlement System (Splitwise)
summary: Design an expense sharing system supporting split strategies (Equal, Exact, Percentage), balance sheet maintenance, and debt simplification.
functionalRequirements: Users can create expenses and split them among group members or individual friends.
Multiple Split Types: Supports EQUAL (split equally), EXACT (specific currency amounts), and PERCENT (percentage of total).
Validation: Ensure sum of exact splits equals total amount; ensure percentages sum to 100%.
Balance Sheet: Tracks who owes whom how much across all transactions.
Debt Simplification: Minimizes the total number of monetary transactions required to settle all debts in a group.
Settlement: Record debt clearance payments between two users.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Extensibility: Adding a new split type (e.g., By Shares or Dynamic Ratios) must be pluggable via Strategy pattern without altering ExpenseService.
Financial Precision: Eliminates floating-point rounding errors using integer cents or high-precision currency types.
Auditability: Historical transactions are immutable; payments append new settlement records.

criteria.name: Split Strategy & Polymorphism
criteria.description: Applies Strategy pattern for split calculations, keeping validation rules cohesive within each strategy.

criteria.name: Balance Sheet & Debt Modeling
criteria.description: Models pairwise balances cleanly without tightly coupling user accounts to raw expense logs.

criteria.name: Precision, Invariants & Edge Cases
criteria.description: Handles rounding cents (e.g. $100 split 3 ways), zero-value splits, and atomic balance updates.

criteria.name: Settlement Graph & Extensibility
criteria.description: Isolates the debt simplification algorithm behind a clear interface, allowing alternative graph solvers.

entities.name: User

entities.name: Group
entities.responsibility: Logical grouping of users sharing recurring expenses

entities.name: Expense
entities.responsibility: Encapsulates payer, total amount, split strategy, and individual split shares

entities.name: Split
entities.responsibility: Value object representing a single user's monetary share in an expense

entities.name: BalanceSheet
entities.responsibility: Maintains net balances owed to and from other users

designPatterns.name: Strategy Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Permits adding new split rules (Equal, Exact, Percent, Share-based) without altering the Expense entity

designPatterns.name: Factory Pattern
designPatterns.justification: Creates the appropriate ISplitStrategy instance based on split type enum

starterTemplate.tradeOffsAndAssumptions: Amounts stored in integer cents to prevent floating point inaccuracies. Debt simplification uses a greedy net-balance min-cash-flow approach.
